findings.title: Client-onboarding mutations run without any `requirePermission` gate
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: routes/client-onboarding-command-center.ts requirePermission on every mutation (:137 create, :154/:200/:247 edit, :177 delete); 403 regression coverage remains in the route suite.

findings.title: `profiles.is_super_admin` is user-writable under the RLS self-update policy (forgeable super-admin flag)
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: supabase/migrations/5302437_protect_is_super_admin.sql installs a BEFORE UPDATE trigger (:14-35) on public.profiles that raises for authenticated/anon JWT roles when is_super_admin changes.

findings.title: `PLATFORM_ADMIN_KEYS` (org traversal) and `ADMIN_BYPASS_KEYS` (permission bypass) are inconsistent trust sets
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: CROSS_TENANT_KEYS vs ELEVATED_TENANT_KEYS split in packages/sdk/src/role-keys.ts; the API re-exports via lib/roles.ts, and catalog-parity.test.ts asserts parity with 5302128.

findings.title: RLS is not a database backstop on API requests (service-role is the default client)
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: rls-startup-check.ts:40-55 refuses prod boot on an empty read allow-list; getScopedClient (services/supabase.ts:197-225) still returns the service-role client for modules not listed in RLS_READS/WRITES_ENABLED and meters the bypass. Residual: deployed allow-list values and write coverage remain operator-side.

findings.title: Write and state-transition actions gated by `view` permissions (action mismatch)
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: the prior single exception remains at routes/ai.ts:217 (POST /triage/analyze uses ai:view), and the training self-service writes were changed to view in this commit - routes/training-hub.ts:227-232 (POST /courses/:id/enroll) and :269-272 (POST /courses/:id/progress) now use requirePermission('training-hub','view'). Both handlers only mutate the caller's own enrollment, so impact is limited, but the write/view mismatch class is broader than before.

findings.title: Webhook endpoint and delivery reads are available to any org member (not manage-gated)
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: routes/webhook-management.ts gates reads with requirePermission('webhooks','view') (:103 list, :125 dead-letters, :348 by-id, :508 deliveries) and mutations with 'webhooks','manage'.

findings.title: API keys store `expires_at` but nothing enforces or prunes expiry
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: expired keys fail closed in middleware/api-key.ts:82-91 and are pruned by the scheduled api-key-prune task (worker/tasks/index.ts:51, schedule-config.ts:50).

findings.title: Webhook signing secrets are stored plaintext with no rotation or expiry
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: routes/webhook-management.ts:35-52 encrypts signing secrets at rest (AES-256-GCM via lib/field-encryption), masks them on read (:28-31,75-78) and records secret_expires_at rotation metadata (:379,441-448; migration 5302441).

findings.title: Profiles are enumerable by email/id for any authenticated user
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: GET /profiles?email=/?ids= still enumerates profiles for any authenticated user (routes/profiles.ts:61-96) but RLS restricts selects to self/same-org/super-admin (5302026:1005-1020) and decryptProfileRow strips ciphertext from responses. Residual: the directory query remains ungated by a users/profiles permission.

findings.title: API-key `permissions` are decorative: keys act with the creator's full permissions and the column is never enforced
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: middleware/permissions.ts:73-80 caps every key request to the stored scope list before creator-side resolution; routes/api-keys.ts:43 gates the list route with api-keys:view.

findings.title: Client-side permission hiding is UI-only for several module actions
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: server enforcement is broad and catalog-linted, but there is still no per-route permission-guard coverage gate; the new ACM-P2-009 records nine module read endpoints that remain org-scoped only, and ACM-P2-003 records the remaining write/view mismatches.

findings.title: No catalog-lint: referenced permission keys are not checked against the `permissions` table
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: scripts/ci/check-permission-catalog.sh runs scripts/check-permission-catalog.mjs over requirePermission literals, live RLS user_has_permission predicates and registerCrud module keys, with a negative fixture; wired in .github/actions/unit-tests/action.yml:121-128.

findings.title: Public route surface is broad and has no single documented inventory
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: docs/PUBLIC_ROUTES.md is generated from the auth:false OpenAPI RouteDefs and CI runs `node scripts/public-route-inventory.mjs --check` (.github/actions/unit-tests/action.yml:133).

findings.title: `GET /roles/:id` and `GET /me/permissions` are readable without an admin gate
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: routes/roles.ts:67 GET /roles/:id now requires requireAdmin; GET /me/permissions remains self-scoped by design (routes/me.ts resolves only req.authUser.userId).

findings.title: RLS policies reference `manage` permissions that no role holds (dead predicates)
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: supabase/migrations/5302459_dead_rls_permission_predicates.sql adds catalog rows for every historical predicate key (tickets:comment/manage, documents:manage/upload, projects:manage, contracts:*, appointments:*, onboarding:update) and the catalog guard is clean.

findings.title: `GET /api-keys` lists org keys for any org member (no `api-keys:view` gate)
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: routes/api-keys.ts:43 GET / requires requirePermission('api-keys','view'); api-keys-list-gate.test.ts covers the denial.

findings.title: AI copilot endpoints have no permission gate (any org member can run summarization and reply drafts)
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: routes/ai.ts gates copilot routes - ai:view on triage list (:346-348), drafts list/detail (:537,562); ai:create on generate/drafts (:418-420,515); ai:edit on review (:578); ai-copilot-permission-gate.test.ts remains.

findings.title: registerCrud reads and final/* module routes have no requirePermission gate
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: apps/api/src/routes/final/crud.ts:31,89 adds requirePermission(permissionModule,'view') to both read routes, and final/sharepoint.ts:9, backups.ts:9,24, budgets.ts:9, procurement.ts:11, time-entries.ts:13 plus routes/sla.ts:17 carry module view gates; final-view-gates.test.ts covers the denials.

findings.title: Module read endpoints are org-scoped but not permission-gated (catalog view grants are UI-only)
findings.note: NEW at 6b7aa1a5: the primary module list/detail routes are mounted with requireAuth+requireOrgAccess only: assets.ts:75, approvals.ts:122, findings.ts:84, proposals.ts:80, qbr.ts:22, vendors.ts:29, service-catalog.ts:20, file-requests.ts:299, domain-monitors.ts:70. Their writes carry create/edit/delete gates, and the catalog defines matching view pairs (5302118:42,134,138,142,256,323,327,331,340), so a role without the view grant can still read by calling the API directly. The clearest over-permission is vendors: catalog scope is 'admin' (:340) yet client-visible vendor contracts are served to client roles through applyClientVisibility (vendors.ts:47-50).
